title: Excision of whole intact mouse brain
author: MacManus
materials: Scalpel handle. Pointed tip scalpel blade. Nitrile gloves (double glove to reduce possibility of stick injury). Phosphate buffer solution or saline solution. Tweezers with rubber tips. Petri dish. Cutting board.

steps.title: Gather required materials
steps.instruction: Collect a scalpel handle, pointed‑tip scalpel blade, double nitrile gloves, phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS) or saline solution, tweezers with rubber tips, a petri dish, and a cutting board.

steps.title: Make sagittal scalp incision
steps.instruction: Using a pointed‑tip scalpel, cut a sagittal incision along the centre of the scalp from the base of the neck to the tip of the snout and resect the scalp; extend the incision posteriorly if more access is needed. Then wash the scalpel blade in sterile PBS or saline to remove hair, blood, and debris.

substeps.instruction: Create sagittal scalp incision from base of neck to tip of snout and resect scalp (extend posteriorly if required).
Wash scalpel blade in sterile PBS or saline to remove debris.

steps.title: Incise cranial bone
steps.instruction: With the same scalpel, incise the cranial bone along the sagittal suture from the intersection of the sagittal and lambdoid sutures to the extremity of the nasal bone, being careful not to cut deeper than the ~0.2 mm thick skull. Then incise laterally across the lambdoid suture.

substeps.instruction: Cut along sagittal suture from sagittal‑lambdoid intersection to nasal bone tip, avoiding deep penetration (skull ≈0.2 mm thick).
Incise laterally across the lambdoid suture.

steps.title: Remove cranial bone segments
steps.instruction: Using the scalpel blade and surgical tweezers, lift and resect each of the three cranial bone segments along the incisions to expose the underlying brain.

steps.title: Detach connective tissue
steps.instruction: Gently resect any connective tissue anchoring the brain to the lower skull cavity with the scalpel; reposition the cadaver on its side or invert it if needed to improve access to inferior tissues.

substeps.instruction: Optionally reposition the cadaver on its side or invert it to aid access to inferior connective tissues.

steps.title: Extract and rinse brain
steps.instruction: Using tweezers with rubber tips, gently remove the intact brain from the cranial vault, place it in a petri dish, and wash it with fresh PBS or saline to remove blood and debris while maintaining hydration. Change the scalpel blade after each excision and wear two pairs of nitrile gloves to prevent sticking injuries.

substeps.instruction: Change scalpel blade after each excision.
Wear two pairs of nitrile gloves throughout the procedure.

steps.title: Inspect brain for damage
steps.instruction: Visually examine the excised brain for any lacerations or damage, especially to the cerebral cortex or olfactory bulbs; discard the brain if any damage is observed.
